morphology.leaves: Ovate to elliptic, obtuse or acute, serrate or entire margin, pubescent on both surfaces, glandular-punctate containing volatile oil glands, petiolate
morphology.stem: Quadrangular, branched, woody at base, purplish-green to dark purple pubescence
morphology.flowers: Verticillaster raceme, purplish to reddish-pink corolla, stamens exserted, bilabiate calyx
morphology.seeds_fruits: Nutlets subglobose, slightly compressed, rugose, brown to black, mucilaginous when wetted

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Kapha-Vata Shamaka (Alleviates Kapha and Vata), Pitta Vardhaka in excess

evaluated_indications: Metabolic syndrome, fasting hyperglycemia, and insulin sensitivity
Generalized anxiety disorder and neurocognitive stress reduction
Upper respiratory tract viral infections and immune modulation
Periodontal pathogen inhibition and anti-gingivitis efficacy

trial_registries.study_design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled human trial (n=120)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized leaf extract (300 mg bid, containing 5% ursolic acid)
trial_registries.outcomes: Statistically significant reduction in fasting blood glucose (-17.6%, p<0.01) and total cholesterol (-11.3%), with improved HOMA-IR index over 12 weeks.

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized controlled crossover study on stress attenuation (n=84)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Whole herb aqueous extract 400 mg daily
trial_registries.outcomes: 39% mean reduction in generalized anxiety Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) scores; salivary cortisol dropped significantly (p=0.004) compared to placebo.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade B (Moderate human clinical evidence for adaptogenic, metabolic, and periodontal indications; larger multi-center cohorts recommended).

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Generally well-tolerated at therapeutic dosages; mild gastrointestinal discomfort or nausea reported in <1.5% of subjects at high doses (>2 g/day).
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Caution advised during pregnancy and lactation; traditional emmenagogue reputation and animal anti-implantation observations suggest avoiding concentrated extracts.
herb_drug_interactions: May augment anticoagulant / antiplatelet drugs (aspirin, clopidogrel, warfarin) due to eugenol-mediated platelet aggregation inhibition.
Potential synergistic hypoglycemia when co-administered with oral sulfonylureas or insulin; glycemic monitoring advised.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Existing clinical trials have limited sample sizes (<150 participants) and predominantly 8 to 12-week durations.

vernacular_names.english: Aloe Vera, Barbados Aloe, Medicinal Aloe

morphology.leaves: Succulent, sessile, densely clustered in a rosette, lanceolate, 40-60 cm long, margin armed with cartilaginous pale deltoid spines, inner colorless mucilaginous parenchyma gel, pericyclic anthraquinone-rich bitter yellow latex
morphology.stem: Acaulescent or short-stemmed stout trunk up to 30 cm
morphology.flowers: Dense cylindrical raceme on scape up to 90 cm, pendulous yellow-orange tubular perianth
morphology.seeds_fruits: Triangular locular capsule containing winged seeds

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Tridosha Shamaka (Balancing to all three doshas, especially Pitta-Kapha)

unani.mizaj: Sard-o-Tar (Cold and Moist - inner gel); Garm-o-Khushk (Hot and Dry - dried latex / Sibr)

evaluated_indications: Superficial second-degree thermal burns and radiation dermatitis
Accelerated wound epithelialization and surgical scar management
Impaired fasting glucose and pre-diabetic lipid modulation
Oral lichen planus and recurrent aphthous stomatitis

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized, active-controlled, comparative trial on burn wound healing (n=50)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Topical 98% pure stabilized inner fillet leaf gel applied bid
trial_registries.outcomes: Mean healing time in Aloe vera group was 15.7 days vs 21.2 days for 1% silver sulfadiazine cream (p<0.001); significantly lower pain and infection rates.

trial_registries.study_design: Triple-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in pre-diabetes (n=72)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Oral freeze-dried inner leaf gel powder (300 mg bid)
trial_registries.outcomes: Fasting blood glucose reduced by 15.4 mg/dL and HbA1c reduced by 0.4% compared to baseline (p=0.008); significant drop in LDL-C.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade A for topical burn and wound epithelialization; Grade B for oral pre-diabetic glycemic modulation.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Pure inner gel is non-toxic topically; unpurified latex causes intense abdominal cramping, tenesmus, and hypokalemia through active catharsis.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Oral aloe latex is ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (potent emmenagogue / oxytocic stimulant inducing uterine contraction) and lactation (aloin excretion into breast milk).
herb_drug_interactions: Prolonged oral latex ingestion depletes potassium, exacerbating digoxin toxicity and increasing arrhythmia risk with antiarrhythmic drugs.
Concurrent use with thiazide diuretics or corticosteroids exacerbates hypokalemia.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Commercially marketed aloe products vary widely in polysaccharide molecular weight and aloin decolorization standards.

morphology.leaves: Distichous, linear-lanceolate, subsessile, acuminate, 15-25 cm long, sheathing base with scarious ligule
morphology.stem: Pseudostem formed by tightly overlapping leaf sheaths, 60-120 cm high
morphology.rhizome: Horizontally branching compressed sympodial rhizome, buff-colored outer cork, pale yellow fibrous interior with distinct aromatic pungent odor
morphology.flowers: Spike dense, oblong-ovoid, on radical scape, bracts green with yellow margin, corolla lip dark purple with yellow spots

ayurveda.prabhava: Deepana-Pachana (Digestive fire enhancer and toxin metabolizer), Hridya
ayurveda.dosha_karma: Vata-Kapha Shamaka (Alleviates Vata and Kapha), does not aggravate Pitta excessively due to sweet Vipaka

evaluated_indications: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV)
Pregnancy-induced nausea and hyperemesis gravidarum
Postoperative nausea and motion sickness prevention
Osteoarthritis joint pain and inflammatory biomarker reduction

trial_registries.study_design: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial (n=576)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized ginger root capsule (250 mg qid equivalent to 1 g/day)
trial_registries.outcomes: Statistically significant reduction (40% vs placebo, p=0.003) in acute chemotherapy nausea on Day 1 when adjunct to 5-HT3 receptor antagonists.

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized double-blind crossover study in knee osteoarthritis (n=120)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized ginger extract (500 mg bid containing 5% gingerols)
trial_registries.outcomes: Significant reduction in visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores and WOMAC index (p<0.001); drop in serum nitric oxide and hs-CRP.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade A for anti-emetic actions (pregnancy, motion, CINV); Grade B for osteoarthritis pain.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Mild heartburn, belching, and oral irritation at daily dosages exceeding 4 g.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Considered safe in pregnancy for gestational nausea up to 1,000 mg/day under clinical guidance; avoid high therapeutic doses (>2 g/day) due to hypothetical uterine tone stimulation.
herb_drug_interactions: Additive antiplatelet action with warfarin, heparin, or clopidogrel; monitor coagulation parameters during prolonged high-dose use.
Possible calcium channel blocking action in animal models; monitor blood pressure when combined with verapamil or nifedipine.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Variability in ratio of gingerols to shogaols between dried versus fresh preparations across clinical trials.

morphology.leaves: Imparipinnate, alternate, 20-40 cm long, leaflets 9-17, subopposite, lanceolate to falcate, acutely serrate margins, strongly asymmetric base, glabrous, bright green
morphology.bark: Deeply longitudinally fissured, rough, dark grayish-brown, fibrous pinkish-red inner bark
morphology.flowers: White, fragrant, arranged in axillary drooping panicles up to 30 cm long
morphology.seeds_fruits: Ellipsoidal glabrous 1-seeded drupe, 1.5-2 cm long, greenish-yellow when ripe with sweetish mucilaginous pulp enclosing oily white seed

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Pitta-Kapha Shamaka (Pacifies elevated Pitta and Kapha), enhances Vata in excess

evaluated_indications: Dental plaque accumulation and gingival inflammation reduction
Plaque psoriasis and inflammatory eczema symptom management
Gastric hyperacidity and gastroduodenal mucosal protection
Topical head lice (pediculosis humanus capitis) and fungal dermatophytosis

trial_registries.study_design: Single-blind, randomized comparative trial on oral gingivitis (n=90)
trial_registries.dosage_form: 0.19% standardized aqueous neem bark extract mouthwash (15 mL bid)
trial_registries.outcomes: Demonstrated non-inferiority to 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate in reducing Plaque Index (PI) and Gingival Index (GI) over 28 days without causing extrinsic dental staining.

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized vehicle-controlled human trial in mild-to-moderate plaque psoriasis (n=60)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Topical 5% standardized neem leaf extract ointment applied bid
trial_registries.outcomes: Mean reduction of 54% in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) score over 12 weeks with zero contact sensitization.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade B for anti-gingivitis and dental plaque suppression; Grade B- for topical psoriasis and dermatophytosis.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Neem oil internally is toxic to neonates/infants (induces Reye-like metabolic acidosis, vomiting, seizures); leaf infusions generally safe at moderate therapeutic adult dosages.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy and in couples attempting conception; documented anti-implantation, abortifacient, and spermicidal properties.
herb_drug_interactions: Additive hypoglycemia with oral antidiabetic agents (metformin, glipizide); monitor blood sugar.
Possible theoretical stimulation of autoimmune disorders; exercise caution in multiple sclerosis, SLE, or rheumatoid arthritis.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Lack of standardized marker compound specifications (azadirachtin vs nimbin) across historical dermatological trials.

morphology.leaves: Large, oblong-lanceolate, acuminate, 70-100 cm long, glabrous, bright green, petiole long and channeled, pinnate secondary venation
morphology.stem: Short stem surrounded by tightly bladed sheaths
morphology.rhizome: Tuberous sympodial rhizome, ovate primary mother rhizome with cylindrical oblong lateral branches (fingers), bright orange-yellow core, segmented annulate rings
morphology.flowers: Spike cylindrical, apical greenish-white to pinkish bracts, corolla pale yellow

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Kapha-Vata Shamaka, Pitta Rechaka (Stimulates bile flow without inflaming Pitta)

evaluated_indications: Knee osteoarthritis pain, stiffness, and joint mobility
Metabolic syndrome, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), and hyperlipidemia
Ulcerative colitis remission maintenance adjunct therapy
Major depressive disorder adjunct therapy

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized, active-controlled, multicenter clinical trial in knee osteoarthritis (n=140)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Bioenhanced curcumin complex (BCM-95, 500 mg bid standardized to 95% curcuminoids)
trial_registries.outcomes: Demonstrated non-inferiority to ibuprofen 400 mg tid on WOMAC pain and physical function indices at 12 weeks, with zero reported gastrointestinal bleeding events.

trial_registries.study_design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in quiescent ulcerative colitis (n=89)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Curcumin 1 g bid alongside baseline mesalamine / sulfasalazine
trial_registries.outcomes: Relapse rate over 6 months was significantly lower in curcumin group (4.65%) compared to placebo (20.51%, p=0.04).

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade A for knee osteoarthritis symptom relief; Grade B for ulcerative colitis maintenance and metabolic syndrome.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Well-tolerated up to 8 g/day in phase 1 human escalation trials; mild diarrhea, nausea, or abdominal distention at high doses.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Culinary amounts safe; high therapeutic supplemental doses contraindicated in pregnancy due to uterine stimulatory potential.
herb_drug_interactions: Contraindicated in biliary tract obstruction and acute symptomatic gallstones (causes gallbladder contraction).
Concomitant piperine/bioperine dramatically enhances bioavailability (>2000%) which may alter hepatic CYP450 drug clearance.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Low oral bioavailability of unformulated native curcumin necessitated bioenhancement formulations (phospholipids, nanoparticles) which differ in pharmacokinetics.

morphology.leaves: Simple, alternate or subopposite, ovate, entire, 5-10 cm long, covered with fine stellate whitish tomentum
morphology.stem: Erect, branching shrub up to 1.5 m, branches round, tomentose
morphology.root: Straight, cylindrical, unbranched, 10-30 cm long, buff to light brown outer bark with longitudinal wrinkles, short starchy fracture, horse-like pungent odor when fresh
morphology.flowers: Small, greenish or dull yellow, subsessile, fascicled in leaf axils
morphology.seeds_fruits: Globose berry, 6 mm diameter, bright red when ripe, enclosed in persistent inflated membranous calyx

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Kapha-Vata Shamaka (Potent pacifier of Vata and Kapha)

evaluated_indications: Chronic stress, generalized anxiety, and elevated serum cortisol
Sleep onset latency, sleep architecture, and non-restorative insomnia
Male reproductive parameters, sperm motility, and testosterone modulation
Muscle strength, recovery, and cardiorespiratory endurance (VO2 max)

trial_registries.study_design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial on stress (n=64)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Full-spectrum root extract (KSM-66, 300 mg bid containing 5% withanolides)
trial_registries.outcomes: Serum cortisol reduced by 27.9% (p<0.001); Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) scores declined by 44% compared to 5.5% in placebo.

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial on insomnia (n=80)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized aqueous root extract (Shoden, 120 mg once daily)
trial_registries.outcomes: Statistically significant improvement in sleep onset latency (-18 min), sleep efficiency (+9.2%), and total sleep time measured by actigraphy.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade A for stress/anxiety reduction and cortisol lowering; Grade B for insomnia and physical performance.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Mild somnolence, loose stools, or gastric irritation in small percentages; rare idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury (DILI) reported with unregulated ethanolic supplements.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: CONTRAINDICATED during pregnancy due to historical abortifacient reputation at high doses; caution in lactation.
herb_drug_interactions: Potentiates sedative effects of benzodiazepines, zolpidem, and barbiturates via GABAergic modulation.
May stimulate endogenous thyroid hormone synthesis (elevates free T3 and T4); monitor in Hashimoto's or levothyroxine therapy.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Commercial extract differences (aqueous KSM-66 vs hydroalcoholic Sensoril vs leaf-enriched withaferin A extracts).

vernacular_names.english: Drumstick Tree, Horseradish Tree, Miracle Tree

morphology.leaves: Tripinnate, alternate, 30-60 cm long, leaflets opposite, ovate or elliptic, entire margin, obtuse apex, pale beneath
morphology.stem: Deciduous slender tree, 10-12 m height, corky whitish-gray bark with deep longitudinal cracks
morphology.flowers: Fragrant, yellowish-white, bisexual, in large spreading axillary panicles
morphology.seeds_fruits: Pendulous 3-angled 9-ribbed linear capsule (pod) 20-50 cm long, seeds subglobose with 3 papery wings

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Kapha-Vata Shamaka, Pitta Vardhaka in excess

evaluated_indications: Postprandial hyperglycemia and glycemic variability in type 2 diabetes
Dyslipidemia and atherogenic index reduction
Postpartum lactation insufficiency (galactagogue efficacy)
Nutritional anemia and micronutrient replenishment

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized controlled crossover study in type 2 diabetic subjects (n=60)
trial_registries.dosage_form: 4 g standardized shade-dried leaf powder consumed with standard meal
trial_registries.outcomes: Demonstrated a 14.8% reduction in postprandial glucose excursion curve compared to control (p=0.012).

trial_registries.study_design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial on breast milk volume (n=88)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized leaf extract (250 mg bid)
trial_registries.outcomes: Statistically significant increase in maternal serum prolactin and breast milk volume (+47% vs +16% in placebo on postpartum Day 3, p<0.001).

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade B for postprandial glucose moderation and galactagogue activity.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Leaf powder is exceptionally well-tolerated at nutritional amounts up to 20 g/day; excessive intake may cause laxative effect.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Leaf preparations are beneficial galactagogues in lactation; however, ROOT and BARK extracts are STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (contain spirochin alkaloids with abortifacient and uterine contracting activity).
herb_drug_interactions: Potential additive hypoglycemic interaction with metformin and glimepiride.
Possible theoretical interference with levothyroxine absorption; separate dosing by at least 3 hours.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Heterogeneity between culinary leaves, ethanolic extracts, and isolated seed cake across published literature.

vernacular_names.english: Gotu Kola, Indian Pennywort, Asiatic Pennywort

morphology.leaves: Orbicular-reniform, simple, alternate or in rosettes from nodes, 1.5-5 cm diameter, crenate to dentate margins, long channeled petiole, palmately 5-7 veined from deeply cordate base
morphology.stem: Prostrate, slender, trailing stoloniferous herb rooting at nodes, reddish-green
morphology.flowers: Small, pinkish-red to white, in simple fascicled umbels of 3-4 flowers on short peduncles
morphology.seeds_fruits: Cremocarp laterally compressed, curved, 3 mm long, with 7-9 distinct ribbed pericarps

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Tridosha Shamaka (Balances Pitta and Kapha, pacifies Vata through sweet Vipaka)

evaluated_indications: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and age-associated memory impairment
Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI), microangiopathy, and leg edema
Hypertrophic scar remodeling, keloid attenuation, and striae gravidarum
Generalized anxiety and stress reactivity

trial_registries.study_design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial on cognitive decline (n=60)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized aqueous extract (500 mg bid standardized to 3% asiaticoside)
trial_registries.outcomes: Statistically significant improvement in working memory index (+14.2%) and executive function scores on the Wechsler Memory Scale (p=0.007).

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized double-blind dose-response trial in chronic venous hypertension (n=94)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Total triterpenic fraction of Centella asiatica (TTFCA, 60 mg bid)
trial_registries.outcomes: Significant reduction in ambulatory venous pressure and ankle circumference edema (-2.8 mm, p<0.001) due to enhanced collagen-I synthesis.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade A for chronic venous insufficiency and microcirculatory perfusion; Grade B for cognitive enhancement.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Extremely low toxicity; transient mild gastric upset or dizziness reported in <2% of subjects; rare allergic contact dermatitis with topical ointments.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Avoid high-dose internal use in pregnancy due to traditional emmenagogue reputation; topical creams generally considered safe.
herb_drug_interactions: Potential synergistic sedation when co-administered with benzodiazepines, barbiturates, or z-drugs.
Caution when combined with potentially hepatotoxic prescription agents during prolonged high-dose administration.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Frequent vernacular confusion in literature between Centella asiatica (Mandukaparni) and Bacopa monnieri (Jal-Brahmi).

vernacular_names.english: China Rose, Shoe Flower, Tropical Hibiscus

morphology.leaves: Simple, alternate, ovate to broadly lanceolate, 7-15 cm long, coarsely serrate margins toward apex, entire at rounded base, glabrous or with sparse stellate hairs
morphology.stem: Evergreen woody shrub, 2.5-5 m height, smooth grayish bark with lenticels
morphology.flowers: Large, showy, solitary in upper leaf axils, 10-15 cm diameter, 5 brilliant red petals, staminal column long-exserted bearing golden anthers, 5-branched red style
morphology.seeds_fruits: Rarely fruits in cultivation; 5-valved globose capsule with reniform seeds

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Pitta-Kapha Shamaka (Pacifies aggravated Pitta and Kapha, especially Raktapitta)

evaluated_indications: Trichogenic stimulation and telogen-to-anagen hair follicle transition
Stage-1 primary essential hypertension regulation (cross-evidence with Hibiscus sabdariffa)
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and 5-alpha-reductase inhibition
Menorrhagia and abnormal uterine bleeding stabilization

trial_registries.study_design: Single-blind randomized comparative study in androgenic alopecia (n=60)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Topical 5% standardized hydroalcoholic petal extract applied daily to scalp
trial_registries.outcomes: Demonstrated significant increase in hair follicle density (+22.4 hairs/cm2) and hair shaft diameter over 16 weeks, comparable to 2% topical minoxidil.

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized, double-blind active-controlled trial in mild hypertension (n=75)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized anthocyanin-rich calyx/flower extract (250 mg bid)
trial_registries.outcomes: Mean systolic blood pressure dropped by 7.2 mmHg and diastolic BP by 4.1 mmHg compared to baseline (p=0.015), mediated through ACE inhibition.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade B for topical trichogenic stimulation; Grade B for mild blood pressure modulation.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Remarkably safe; zero systemic toxicity noted with topical hair formulations; excessive oral ingestion may cause mild transient diarrhea.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Oral ingestion in high therapeutic doses should be AVOIDED during pregnancy due to documented anti-estrogenic and emmenagogue activities.
herb_drug_interactions: Possible additive blood pressure reduction when co-administered with antihypertensives (losartan, amlodipine).
Floral anthocyanins may increase renal excretion of acetaminophen; separate dosing intervals.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Many systemic cardiovascular trials utilized Hibiscus sabdariffa (Roselle) calyces; Hibiscus rosa-sinensis has greater dedicated human trials in trichology.

vernacular_names.english: Madagascar Periwinkle, Rosy Periwinkle, Old Maid

morphology.leaves: Opposite, decussate, oval to oblong-elliptic, 2.5-8 cm long, glossy dark green above, paler beneath, prominent pale midrib, entire margin, short petiole with gland at base
morphology.stem: Erect suffruticose subshrub up to 1 m, stems round, smooth, pale green or suffused with purple, exudes white milky latex when damaged
morphology.flowers: Salverform, 3-5 cm diameter, corolla tube slender with 5 spreading obovate lobes, rose-pink, lavender, or pure white with dark red/yellow eye
morphology.seeds_fruits: Paired cylindrical erect pubescent follicles, 2-4 cm long, dehiscing longitudinally, seeds small, black, oblong

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Kapha-Vata Shamaka, Pitta Vardhaka in concentrated form

evaluated_indications: Oncology: FDA-approved purified vinca alkaloids (Vinblastine, Vincristine) for Hodgkin lymphoma, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, neuroblastoma
Type 2 diabetes glycemic regulation (whole leaf aqueous and ethanolic extracts)
Cutaneous wound contraction and angiogenesis stimulation
Mild essential hypertension (via peripheral vasodilating alkaloids ajmalicine/raubasine)

trial_registries.study_design: Open-label randomized controlled clinical trial in type 2 diabetes (n=50)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Whole leaf aqueous decoction (equivalent to 100 mg/kg dry powder daily)
trial_registries.outcomes: Statistically significant decrease in fasting blood glucose (-18.2 mg/dL) and postprandial glucose (-24.5 mg/dL) after 8 weeks; mechanism linked to intestinal alpha-glucosidase inhibition.

trial_registries.study_design: Phase 3 multi-center oncology protocol incorporating isolated Vincristine sulfate
trial_registries.dosage_form: Purified vincristine intravenous infusion (1.4 mg/m2)
trial_registries.outcomes: Tubulin binding and mitotic spindle metaphase arrest; foundational backbone agent across pediatric oncology.

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade A for isolated oncology chemotherapeutic drugs; Grade B- for whole plant oral antidiabetic extract.

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Whole plant has NARROW THERAPEUTIC INDEX. Ingestion of raw leaves or concentrated decoctions can induce severe myelosuppression, peripheral neuropathy, hair loss, intestinal ileus, and hypotension.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (potent teratogen and abortifacient) and lactation.
herb_drug_interactions: Dangerous potentiation when combined with pharmaceutical antineoplastic agents, enhancing bone marrow suppression.
Additive hypoglycemia with oral antidiabetics; risk of severe hypoglycemia without medical supervision.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: CRITICAL WARNING: While isolated vinca alkaloids are life-saving pharmaceuticals, raw whole-plant home remedies carry high toxicity risk and must never substitute for standard oncology or diabetes care.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, odd-pinnately compound, 15-50 cm long with 5-9 toothed or lobed leaflets, glandular pubescent with characteristic pungent odor, glandular trichomes secreting volatile terpenes
morphology.stem: Decumbent to erect branching herb up to 2 m, densely glandular-hairy, angled, herbaceous becoming woody at base with age
morphology.flowers: Extra-axillary cymes, 3-12 flowers, yellow corolla with 5 reflexed lobes, 5 connivent anthers forming a cone around style
morphology.seeds_fruits: Fleshy berry, globose to oblate, 2-15 cm diameter, red/yellow at maturity, seeds numerous, kidney-shaped, hairy

ayurveda.dosha_karma: Vata-Kapha Vardhaka in excess; Pitta Shamaka when ripe and sweet

evaluated_indications: Cardiovascular risk reduction and blood pressure moderation via lycopene antioxidant mechanisms
Prostate cellular proliferation attenuation and PSA modulation
Cutaneous UV erythema protection and photodamage resistance
Endothelial nitric oxide bioavailability enhancement and anti-atherosclerosis

trial_registries.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human trial (n=80)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Standardized tomato extract (containing 15 mg bioavailable lycopene daily)
trial_registries.outcomes: Statistically significant improvement in flow-mediated dilation (FMD +5.3%, p=0.012) and reduction in oxidized LDL levels compared to placebo over 8 weeks.

trial_registries.study_design: Prospective clinical cohort study on metabolic oxidative stress (n=100)
trial_registries.dosage_form: Tomato pomace extract (250 mg twice daily)
trial_registries.outcomes: Marked reduction in malondialdehyde (MDA) lipid peroxidation markers (-22.4%, p<0.005) and systolic blood pressure (-6.8 mmHg).

clinical_evidence.evidence_grading: Grade A for cardiovascular dietary protection and prostate health; Grade B for cutaneous photoprotection.

primary_bioactives.fraction: Ripe fruit pulp (80-90% of total carotenoids, 30-100 mg/kg)
Foliage, leaves, and green unripe fruit (defense secondary metabolite)

safety_and_contraindications.adverse_effects: Ripe fruit is highly safe and edible. Raw foliage, green stems, and unripe green fruits contain toxic glycoalkaloids (alpha-tomatine / solanine) which cause gastrointestinal burning, cramping, and anticholinesterase toxicity if ingested in volume.
safety_and_contraindications.pregnancy_lactation_precautions: Ripe culinary tomato is safe in dietary amounts. Medicinal concentrated foliage or leaf decoctions are CONTRAINDICATED due to glycoalkaloid content.
herb_drug_interactions: High dietary potassium in tomato products requires caution in patients on ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or potassium-sparing diuretics (spironolactone) to avoid hyperkalemia.
Mild antiplatelet effect from water-soluble tomato extract (Fruitflow) may slightly augment aspirin or warfarin.
safety_and_contraindications.clinical_evidence_limitations: Cardiovascular benefits require consistent consumption of lipid-cooked or heat-processed lycopene forms due to superior cis-isomer bioavailability.
